hints: Every crate takes exactly one slot in the van no matter its type. So which crates deserve the slots first?
Greedy by value: sort crate types by itemsPerCrate descending and take as many of the richest type as possible before moving on.

1. Sort crate types by itemsPerCrate, largest first.
  2. For each type: take = min(count, capacity left).
  3. Add take × itemsPerCrate to the total; subtract take from capacity.
  4. Stop when capacity is 0; return the total.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Expand every crate individually, sort all of them by items, and take the top capacity.
approaches.time: O(C log C) where C = total crates

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sort the crate types (not individual crates) by items per crate and fill greedily.

explain: Sample 1: types sorted are [1,6],[2,4],[3,1], capacity 4. Take 1 crate of 6 (total 6, 3 left), then 2 crates of 4 (total 14, 1 left), then 1 crate of 1 (total 15). Since every crate costs the same one slot, swapping a poorer crate for a richer one can only help, so greedy is optimal. Edge case: capacity larger than all crates — just take everything.
recognize: Fixed-size slots and items of different values with no other constraint → sort by value and fill greedily.
